title: The first millennium BCE, 1000 BCE–1 CE
reviewed: 2026-10-18. Each quote was copied from the linked article and is checked by npm run verify:sources.

events.title: Ashurbanipal gathers his library at Nineveh
events.summary: The Assyrian king collects clay tablets on every subject. More than 30,000 tablets and fragments survive.

source.quote: King Ashurbanipal (668–627 BCE)

events.title: Nineveh falls and Assyria ends
events.summary: An alliance of Babylonians and Medes sacks the Assyrian capital. The Assyrian Empire soon collapses.

source.quote: the Conquest of the Assyrian Empire in 612 BC

events.title: Cyrus the Great founds the Persian Empire
events.summary: Cyrus of Persia founds the Achaemenid Empire. Its kings come to rule from Egypt to the Indus.

source.quote: founded by Cyrus the Great of the Achaemenid dynasty in 550 BC

events.title: Building begins at Persepolis
events.summary: Persian kings begin a great ceremonial capital. Alexander's army burns its palaces in 330 BCE.

quote: The earliest remains of Persepolis date back to 515 BC.
taken by the army of Alexander the Great in 330 BC

events.title: Alexander the Great invades the Persian Empire
events.summary: Alexander of Macedon crosses into Asia and conquers the Persian Empire. He dies at Babylon in 323 BCE.

quote: invasion of the Achaemenid Persian Empire in 334 BC

events.title: Seleucus founds the Seleucid Empire
events.summary: One of Alexander's generals takes the eastern part of his empire. His dynasty rules from Mesopotamia to Syria.

source.quote: Seleucus I Nicator in 312 BC

events.title: The Parthian Empire rises in Iran
events.summary: The Arsacid dynasty founds an Iranian empire. It later becomes Rome's great rival in the east.

source.quote: from 247 BC to 224 AD

events.title: The first Olympic Games
events.summary: Greek tradition dates the first games at Olympia to this year.

source.quote: traditionally dated to 776 BC

events.title: The traditional founding of Rome
events.summary: Roman tradition sets the city's founding in this year. Archaeology shows earlier villages on its hills.

source.quote: placing Rome's founding in 753 BC

events.title: Cleisthenes reforms Athens into a democracy
events.summary: Cleisthenes gives power to an assembly of citizens. Athenian democracy grows from these reforms.

source.quote: Cleisthenes (in 508–07 BC)

events.title: Athens defeats Persia at Marathon
events.summary: Athenian soldiers defeat the first Persian invasion of Greece.

source.quote: took place in 490 BCE during the first Persian invasion of Greece

events.title: The Parthenon is built
events.summary: Athens builds a temple to Athena on the Acropolis. It thanks the goddess for victory over Persia.

events.title: The La Tène culture of the Celts
events.summary: A Celtic Iron Age culture spreads across much of Europe. It lasts until the Roman conquest.

source.quote: from about 450 BC to the Roman conquest in the 1st century BC

events.title: Hannibal crosses the Alps
events.summary: The Carthaginian general leads his army and elephants over the Alps into Italy.

source.quote: Hannibal's crossing of the Alps in 218 BC

events.title: Julius Caesar is assassinated
events.summary: Senators kill the Roman dictator during a Senate session. Civil war follows.

source.quote: the Ides of March (15 March), 44 BC

events.title: Augustus becomes the first Roman emperor
events.summary: Octavian takes the name Augustus and rules as emperor. The Roman Republic gives way to the Empire.

source.quote: the first Roman emperor from 27 BC

events.title: The Scythians rule the western steppe
events.summary: Mounted Scythian nomads become the dominant power on the western Eurasian steppe.

source.quote: the dominant power on the western Eurasian Steppe in the 8th century BC

events.title: Phoenicians from Tyre settle Carthage
events.summary: Merchants from Tyre found Carthage in North Africa. It grows into a great sea power.

source.quote: Carthage was settled around 814 BC by merchants from Tyre

events.title: Kushite kings rule Egypt
events.summary: Kings from Kush in Nubia rule Egypt as its Twenty-fifth Dynasty for nearly a century.

source.quote: from 744 to 656 BC

events.title: Meroë becomes the capital of Kush
events.summary: The Kingdom of Kush rules from Meroë on the Nile for centuries.

source.quote: for several centuries from around 590 BC

events.title: The Library of Alexandria flourishes
events.summary: Scholars gather at the great library of Ptolemaic Egypt. They study Homer, mathematics, and the stars.

source.quote: during the third and second centuries BC

events.title: Djenné-Djenno grows on the Niger
events.summary: People settle a site in the inland Niger delta. It becomes one of West Africa's oldest towns.

source.quote: occupied from 250 BC to 1400 AD

events.title: The Buddha teaches in northern India
events.summary: A wandering teacher in the Ganges plain founds Buddhism. Scholars debate the exact years of his life.

source.quote: during the 6th or 5th century BCE and founded Buddhism

events.title: The Maurya Empire unites much of India
events.summary: Chandragupta Maurya founds an empire across northern India. It is one of the largest in Indian history.

source.quote: 320 BCE, it existed in loose-knit fashion until 185 BCE

events.title: Ashoka carves his edicts
events.summary: The Maurya emperor Ashoka has moral teachings carved on pillars and rocks across India.

events.title: The Zhou court moves east
events.summary: The Eastern Zhou period begins. Local lords gain power as royal power weakens.

events.title: Confucius teaches in Lu
events.summary: The philosopher Kong Qiu teaches ethics and good government. His ideas shape China for millennia.

events.title: Qin unifies China
events.summary: The state of Qin conquers its rivals. Its king becomes the first emperor of China.

source.quote: in 221 BC with the successful unification of China

events.title: The Terracotta Army is buried
events.summary: Thousands of clay soldiers are buried with the first emperor to guard him after death.

source.quote: buried with the emperor in 210–209 BCE

events.title: The Han dynasty begins
events.summary: Liu Bang founds the Han dynasty after the fall of Qin. Han rule lasts about four centuries.

source.quote: The Han dynasty (202 BC – 9 AD, 25–220 AD)

events.title: Modu Chanyu founds the Xiongnu Empire
events.summary: Nomads of the eastern steppe unite under one leader. They become a great rival of Han China.

source.quote: Modu Chanyu, the supreme leader after 209 BC, founded the Xiongnu Empire.

events.title: Zhang Qian's missions open Silk Road routes
events.summary: A Han envoy's journeys to Central Asia open trade routes to the west.

source.quote: expanded around 114 BC largely through the missions

events.title: The Yayoi period begins in Japan
events.summary: Rice farming and metalwork spread across the Japanese islands. Some scholars date the start earlier.

quote: accepted to date from circa 300 BC to AD 300
from around the 10th century BC or 9th–8th century BC

events.title: La Venta becomes the Olmec center
events.summary: After San Lorenzo declines, La Venta becomes the main Olmec city. Its people carve colossal heads.

events.title: The temple center of Chavín de Huántar
events.summary: A religious center in the Peruvian Andes draws pilgrims from a wide region.

events.title: The Paracas culture on the Peruvian coast
events.summary: An Andean society in southern Peru weaves some of the finest ancient textiles.

source.quote: between approximately 800 BCE and 100 BCE

events.title: El Mirador, a great Preclassic Maya city
events.summary: The Maya build huge temples at El Mirador in the Petén. It peaks from the 3rd century BCE.

source.quote: flourished from about the 6th century BC to the 1st century AD

events.title: Monte Albán is founded
events.summary: The Zapotec build a hilltop city in the Oaxaca valley. It becomes their capital.

source.quote: Founded toward the end of the Middle Formative period at around 500 BC

events.title: The Adena mound builders
events.summary: Woodland peoples in the Ohio valley build burial mounds and earthworks.

source.quote: existed from 500 BC to 100 AD

events.title: Lapita voyagers settle Tonga
events.summary: Seafarers of the Lapita culture reach Tonga. It is the first island settled in Polynesia.

source.quote: By 2850 BP (900 BC) they were already in Tonga
